([[Raleigh, North Carolina]]) | college = [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] (2016–2018) | draft_year = 2018 | career_start = 2018 | years1 = {{nbay|2018|full=y}} | team1 = [[Chicago Bulls]] | years2 = 2018–2019 | team2 = →[[Windy City Bulls]] | years3 = 2020 | team3 = [[FC Porto (basketball)|FC Porto]] | years4 = 2021 | team4 = [[Raptors 905]] | years5 = 2021 | team5 = [[Gießen 46ers]] | years6 = 2021–2022 | team6 = [[Riesen Ludwigsburg]] | years7 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team7 = [[Salt Lake City Stars]] | years10 = 2023–2024 | team10 = [[Ironi Ness Ziona B.C.|Ironi Ness Ziona]] | years11 = 2024 | team11 = [[Aris B.C.|Aris Thessaloniki]] | years12 = 2024–present | team12 = [[Hapoel Galil Elyon]] | highlights = *[[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] All-Freshman Team (2017) }} '''Rawle Prince Alkins''' (born October 29, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Hapoel Galil Elyon]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. He played in the [[NBA]] for the [[Chicago Bulls]] in 2018–19. ==High school career== Alkins first attended [[Christ the King Regional High School]] in [[Queens, New York]] for three years, where he led them to three New York state catholic championships. After his junior year, Alkins decided to attend [[Word of God Christian Academy]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]] for his senior year. As a senior, he averaged 25 points and 7 rebounds per game. Alkins was rated as a five-star recruit and considered a top-20 recruit in the 2016 high school class. He was ranked No. 21 recruit and the 5th best small forward in the Class of 2016 by ESPN, behind [[Josh Jackson (basketball)|Josh Jackson]], [[Jayson Tatum]], [[Miles Bridges]], and [[Jonathan Isaac]]. ==College career== As a freshman, Alkins averaged 10.9 points, 4.9 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game and shot 37 percent from 3-point range. He declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]] but opted to return to Arizona.{{cite news|last1=Parrish|first1=Gary|title=Rawle Alkins withdraws from NBA Draft to return to Arizona for sophomore season|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/rawle-alkins-withdraws-from-nba-draft-to-return-to-arizona-for-sophomore-season/|accessdate=March 23, 2018|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=May 21, 2017}} He missed some games in January 2018 with a broken foot.{{cite news|last1=Pascoe|first1=Bruce|title=Seen and heard at Beasley Coliseum: Rawle Alkins heats up, Lorenzo Romar plays grandpa|url=http://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/seen-and-heard-at-beasley-coliseum-rawle-alkins-heats-up/collection_4c9b5bdc-0712-11e8-ac7f-77206b9a2cf4.html#anchor_item_1|accessdate=March 23, 2018|work=Arizona Daily Star|date=January 31, 2018}} As a sophomore, Alkins averaged 13.1 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game.{{cite news|last1=Boan|first1=Christopher|title=Arizona Basketball: Dusan Ristic, Rawle Alkins ready for one last Dance|url=https://www.tucsonweekly.com/TheRange/archives/2018/03/15/arizona-basketball-dusan-ristic-rawle-alkins-ready-for-one-last-dance|accessdate=March 23, 2018|work=Tucson Weekly|date=March 15, 2018}} On March 27, 2018, Alkins declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] and hired an agent, forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.{{cite news|last1=Johnson|first1=Raphielle|title=Arizona SG Rawle Alkins to enter 2018 NBA Draft|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/03/27/arizona-sg-rawle-alkins-to-enter-2018-nba-draft/|accessdate=March 29, 2018|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=March 27, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2018–2019)=== After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Alkins signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]] for their Summer League team.{{Cite web|url=https://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2018/06/22/report-raptors-agree-to-camp-deal-with-rawle-alkins/,%20https://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2018/06/22/report-raptors-agree-to-camp-deal-with-rawle-alkins/|title=Report: Raptors agree to camp deal with Rawle Alkins - Raptors Republic|first=Blake|last=Murphy|date=June 22, 2018|website=www.raptorsrepublic.com}} After completing his stint there, his performances led to him signing a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Chicago Bulls]] on July 25. With this contract, he split his playing time for the season between the Chicago Bulls and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Windy City Bulls]]. Alkins made his NBA debut on December 17, 2018, playing three minutes with a rebound and two assists in a 121–96 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyherald.com/sports/20181217/lightning-doesnt-strike-twice-for-feisty-bulls-in-okc|title=Lightning doesn't strike twice for feisty Bulls in OKC|first=Mike|last=McGraw|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights)|Daily Herald]]|date=December 17, 2018|access-date=December 19, 2018}} He made 10 NBA appearances for the Bulls, with averages of 3.7 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. He made 44 appearances in the G League with the Windy City Bulls. In those games he averaged 11.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 2.9 assists, primarily off the bench. Alkins, was waived at the end of the season. Alkins was with [[Houston Rockets]] for [[2019 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/summerleague/2019/players?team=rockets&league=vegas|title=NBA SUMMER LEAGUE PLAYERS|website=NBA.com|accessdate=July 4, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.wildcat.arizona.edu/article/2019/07/rawle-alkins-getting-ready-for-year-two-promises-to-be-improved-version-of-himself|title=Rawle Alkins getting ready for year two, promises to be 'improved version of himself'|date=July 8, 2019|website=arizona.edu|accessdate=July 8, 2019}} ===FC Porto (2020)=== On February 26, 2020, Alkins signed with [[FC Porto (basketball)|FC Porto]] of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol]] (LPB).{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcporto.pt/pt/noticias/20200226-pt-rawle-alkins-assina-ate-ao-final-da-epoca|title=Rawle Alkins assina até ao final da é+oca|last=|first=|date=February 26, 2020|website=|publisher=fcporto.pr|language=Portuguese|access-date=February 26, 2020}} He only featured in 2 contests, due to the season suspension, and averaged 16 points, 3 rebounds, 2.5 assists, and 1 steal. On December 4, 2020, Alkins signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]].{{cite web |title=Pelicans sign Rawle Alkins |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-rawle-alkins |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 5, 2020 |date=December 4, 2020}} He was waived at the end of training camp and signed by the [[Birmingham Squadron|Erie BayHawks]]. However, he was waived on January 26, 2021, without making an appearance for them.{{cite web |title=ERIE BAYHAWKS MAKE TWO ROSTER MOVES |url=https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/erie-bayhawks-make-two-roster-moves/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 1, 2021 |date=January 26, 2021}} ===Raptors 905 (2021)=== On March 3, 2021, Alkins signed with the [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA G League]], the affiliate team of the NBA's [[Toronto Raptors]]. In 3 games for the 905, Alkins averaged 2.7 points, 0.3 rebounds and 0.3 steals. ===Gießen 46ers (2021)=== On September 3, 2021, he signed with [[Gießen 46ers]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/rawle-alkins-joins-giessen-46ers/|title=Rawle Alkins joins Giessen 46ers|last=|first=|date=September 3, 2021|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 3, 2021}} In two games, Alkins averaged 15 points, three rebounds, one steal and one block per game. ===MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg (2021–2022)=== On October 7, 2021, Alkins signed with [[Riesen Ludwigsburg|MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{cite web |title=Rawle Alkins is a newcomer at Ludwigsburg |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Germany/news/708068/Rawle-Alkins-is-a-newcomer-at-Ludwigsburg |website=Eurobasket |access-date=October 7, 2021 |date=October 7, 2021}} He averaged 8.9 points and 2.3 rebounds.{{Cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/slc-stars-acquire-rights-to-rawle-alkins-and-2022-second-round-draft-pick/n-5884078|title=SLC Stars Acquire Rights to Rawle Alkins and 2022 Second Round Draft Pick|date=September 21, 2022|website=OurSports Central}} ===Salt Lake City Stars (2022–2023)=== On October 23, 2022, Alkins joined the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] training camp roster.{{cite web|title=Stars Announce 2022-23 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/stars-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster/n-5892964|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=October 23, 2022}} ===Ironi Ness Ziona (2023–2024)=== In November 2023, Alkins signed with [[Ironi Ness Ziona B.C.|Ironi Ness Ziona]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite tweet|author=Sports Rabbi|title=Rawle Alkins joins Nes Ziona for the 23/24 season. The @ArizonaMBB guard played in the NBA with the Bulls and has also featured in Germany, Portugal and the G-League. Good Luck @Iam_RawleAlkins, Welcome to @ironinessziona & Israel🇮🇱!|number=1724081633144242352|user=thesportsrabbi|date=November 13, 2023|access-date=January 26, 2024}} ==Personal life== Alkins grew up
